methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Mithril Mining operates in the Climate & Energy sector at an undisclosed stage. The valuation universe comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. This narrow peer set limits traditional benchmarking precision.

Peer-median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient clustering. Of the eight same-sector peers identified, none satisfied narrow filtering criteria—no matches emerged for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier cohorts. A minimum of three datapoints is required for reliable peer-median analysis; the filtered set yielded zero. Applying the full eight-peer median would introduce significant comparability noise given heterogeneity in stage and scale across the Climate & Energy landscape.

Given these constraints, a triangulated valuation cannot be supported by the available data. Any meaningful analysis would require either: disclosure of the target's funding stage and recent valuation to enable tighter peer segmentation, or expansion of the comparable universe to include cross-sector frontier-tech companies at demonstrable stage parity. Until then, reliance on public market signals (LNZA) or direct fundraising documentation remains the most defensible approach. The sector's rapid innovation cycles and capital intensity further amplify uncertainty in forward-looking multiples.
